paragraphs.text: Ball lightning is a glowing ball sometimes seen during thunderstorms, usually lasting a few seconds, and still unexplained by science. This review gathers 41 eyewitness reports from scientists and other trained observers, from eight countries, between 1868 and 2020. The author says the collection does not claim to be complete.

paragraphs.text: Ball lightning is very hard to catch on camera or with instruments. One search of about 12,000 night-sky photos found only two likely events. So careful reports from people trained to observe are especially valuable.

paragraphs.text: Reported sizes ranged from 1.5 centimetres to 15 metres, with most under 20 centimetres. About 73 percent appeared during thunderstorms, and 41 percent of witnesses saw a lightning stroke at the same moment. The cases vary so much that some are hard to fit into one explanation, which has led some researchers to suggest several types may exist.

fuller.text: Ball lightning is a glowing ball sometimes seen during thunderstorms, usually lasting a few seconds, and science still cannot explain it. This review gathers 41 sightings reported by scientists and other trained observers, such as weather station staff, from eight countries between 1868 and 2020. It also describes six famous or unusual cases, and it does not claim to be a complete list.

It also describes six famous or unusual cases, and it does not claim to be a complete list.

fuller.text: There are thousands of eyewitness reports, but almost no instrument recordings, because the event appears randomly and briefly. One search of about 12,000 night-sky photos taken over ten years found only two probable cases. So reports from people trained to observe carefully are seen as a promising source of good evidence.

fuller.text: In this small sample, reported sizes ranged from 1.5 cm to 15 m, with most under 20 cm. Sightings lasted from 1.5 to 180 seconds, most often under 3 seconds. About 73% happened during a thunderstorm, and 41% of witnesses saw a lightning strike at the same moment.

brief.text: Ball lightning is a rare glowing ball that sometimes appears during thunderstorms, then vanishes within seconds. There are thousands of reports of it, but almost no recordings, and no one agrees on what causes it. Because it is so hard to catch on camera, this review gathers sightings by scientists and other trained observers.

sentences.text: Ball lightning is a rare glowing ball that sometimes appears during thunderstorms, then vanishes within seconds.
There are thousands of reports of it, but almost no recordings, and no one agrees on what causes it.
Because it is so hard to catch on camera, this review gathers sightings by scientists and other trained observers.

brief.text: It collects 41 such reports from eight countries, from 1868 to 2020. The balls varied widely in size, how long they lasted, and where they appeared, so one simple explanation may not fit them all. The author concludes that careful reports like these can guide future study and help test ideas about ball lightning.
